nh_dartmouth_lake_sunapee.blurb: This stretch of west-central New Hampshire runs from Lake Sunapee north toward Dartmouth College at Hanover, with I-89 passing through it. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, mainly in the V0 to V4 range with a few much harder problems, alongside a smaller set of sport, trad and top-rope lines that mostly sit between 5.6 and 5.11. Pickledish holds the most climbs, followed by the Newbury Cut, a railroad cut dating to 1872 whose blasted, blocky holds make the bolted lines feel unusual. Dragon's Pass and Near and Bald Mountain Woods add more boulders and short routes. The area is spread over many small crags and individual boulders rather than one big cliff.

or_madrone_wall.blurb: Madrone Wall is a county park near Damascus, Oregon, where a 120-foot basalt wall cuts across the property with views toward the Clackamas River; the park takes its name from the madrone trees growing around it. Trad climbing leads here, with a smaller set of sport lines, and the grades cluster in the 5.10 and 5.11 range with a modest number of easier routes below. Hardscrabble Wall and Main Wall hold the most climbs, followed by Shining Wall and Orange Wall, so the cliff is split into several faces that sit close together.

sd_breezy_point.blurb: Breezy Point sits in the Black Hills of South Dakota, within the Mount Rushmore National Memorial, at roughly 5,200 feet. The approach to the cliffs is short, around five minutes. Climbing is split fairly evenly between boulder problems, sport lines and trad lines, with roped routes up to about 100 feet. Most roped climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.11, while the boulders run from V0 up to about V9. Breezy Point Boulders holds the most climbs. Hall Of Truth Corridor is mostly sport, Sentinel Rock is mostly trad, and West World adds more routes.

tn_suck_creek_canyon.blurb: Suck Creek Canyon is a trad-leaning area close to Chattanooga, Tennessee, with some sport and aid climbing mixed in. Climbs are mostly 5.8 to 5.12, with the greatest number around 5.10. The canyon is known for longer routes, including some three-pitch lines, and for an alpine-style feel. The stone is variable, and loose or rotten sections turn up on some routes. The Camp holds the most climbs, followed by Roadside Wall, Upper Passes and Flying Squirrel Buttress.

ut_echo_canyon.blurb: Echo Canyon lies in the Wasatch Back of Utah, with its walls north of I-80, mostly facing southwest through southeast. The rock is conglomerate, and the climbing is bolted cobble work on pockets, slopers, crimps and jugs. Sport routes make up nearly everything, running from about 5.10 to 5.13 with the largest group around 5.12. Mill Canyon and Bear Hollow hold the most climbs, followed by The Dry Wall and Roadside Crag. Bear Hollow has a good number of moderates, in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, with short approaches.

vt_dekd_killington.blurb: DEKD Killington is a bouldering area in Killington, in Central Vermont, where erratic boulders left behind by glaciers are scattered through the woods on and below a ridge, with the Appalachian Trail passing several of the first ones. Every climb is a boulder problem, and the grades lean easy: plenty of V0 to V3, some V4 and V5, and a few hard problems around V7 and V8. Dr. Evil's Lair, Right Ridge and Western Frontier hold the most climbs, and Dirty Crack Boulder is one of many single-boulder crags in between.
